hints.title: Non-Overlapping Interval Profit Maximization Obstacle
hints.text: Each job has a start time, end time, and profit, and chosen jobs cannot overlap. How can sorting jobs by end time and finding the latest compatible predecessor job maximize cumulative profit?

hints.title: Compatible Job Binary Search Invariant
hints.text: For a job ending at E with profit P and start time S, the maximum profit including this job is P plus the maximum profit achievable among jobs ending on or before S.

hints.title: Sorted End Time Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Zip and sort jobs by end time. Maintain an array of end-time and cumulative-profit pairs initialized with [0, 0]. For each job (start, end, profit), bisect the end times to find the latest job finishing at or before start. If that prior profit + current profit exceeds the latest recorded profit, append (end, new_profit). Return the final recorded profit.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N); for each job, bisection takes O(log N).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching without ordered bisection evaluates 2^N schedules.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of (endTime, profit) pairs consumes linear space O(N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorting by end time and using bisection to quickly locate the latest compatible job.
